evidence.excerpt: The relationship between the current control loop bandwidth of grid-following single-phase inverters and their conducted emission characteristics in the 150 kHz to 2 MHz range is examined through a parametric simulation study validated by laboratory measurements. A full-cycle time-domain inverter model is implemented in PLECS and exercised across current controller bandwidths from 500 Hz to 8 kHz, LCL filter corner frequencies from 4 kHz to 20 kHz, and DC bus voltages of 200 V, 350 V and 600 V. Conducted emission spectra at the AC terminals are extracted via an embedded LISN model and compared with CISPR 11 Class B limits. Increasing controller bandwidth from 1 kHz to 5 kHz reduces low-frequency distortion but increases emissions in the 200 kHz to 600 kHz band by 3 to 11 dB depending on LCL corner frequency. A low-pass post-filter of 47 µH/10 nF placed after the LCL filter reduces peak emission levels by 8 dB with less than 0.3% increase in fundamental voltage drop. Laboratory validation on a 2 kW prototype confirms simulation trends with deviations below 4 dB across 90% of the measured frequency range.
